fields.vision: Moved by the Spirit of the Risen Christ, La Consolacion University Philippines, envisions itself to become a catalyst for the wholistic transformational development of Catholic Augustinian Marian graduates rooted in Gospel values.
fields.egas:
EGA 1: Critical and Creative thinker
EGA 2: Competent Catholic Augustinian- Marian Professional
EGA 3: Socially Responsive Steward
EGA 4: Transformative Lifelong learner
fields.pos:
PO1. Ability to apply knowledge of mathematics and science to solve complex engineering problems;
PO2. Ability to design and conduct experiments, as well as to analyze and interpret data.
PO3. Ability to design a system, component, or process to meet desired needs within realistic constraints such as economic, environmental, social, political, ethical, health and safety, manufacturability and sustainability, in accordance with standards.
PO4. Ability to function on multidisciplinary teams;
PO5. Ability to identify; formulate, and solve complex engineering problems.
PO6. Understanding of professional and ethical responsibility.
PO7. Ability to communicate effectively.
PO8. Broad education necessary to understand the impact of engineering
solutions in a global, economic, environmental, and societal context.
PO9. Recognition of the need for, and an ability to engage in life-long learning;
PO10. Knowledge of contemporary issues.
PO11. Ability to use techniques, skills and modern engineering tools necessary for engineering practice; and
PO12. Knowledge and understanding of engineering and management principles as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.
PO13: Ability to design, develop, implement and improve integrated system that include people materials, implementation, equipment and energy.

CLO1: Apply interdisciplinary knowledge from computing, mathematics, physical and social sciences to identify, formulate, and solve complex engineering problems through the design and execution of experiments, and the development of systems or processes that meet real-world needs within economic, environmental, social, political, ethical, health and safety, manufacturability, and sustainability constraints, in accordance with professional standards. (EGA 1) (PO 1, 2, 3, 5)

and collaborate within multidisciplinary teams, guided by Catholic Augustinian-Marian values. (EGA2) (PO 6, 7, 12)

(EGA 4 ) (PO 10, 11, 13)

fields.title: Operation Management
fields.description:
This course provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the principles, strategies, and tools used in
managing operations within manufacturing and service organizations. It explores key topics such as operations strategy,
process design, capacity planning, supply chain management, inventory control, quality assurance, and project scheduling.
Emphasis is placed on applying quantitative and qualitative methods to solve real-world operational challenges, improve
productivity, and enhance organizational competitiveness. Through case studies, simulations, and team projects, students
will develop critical thinking and decision-making skills essential for effective operations leadership in dynamic business
environments.
Anchored in Marian and Augustinian values, this course introduces students to the principles and tools of managing
operations in manufacturing and service organizations. It emphasizes strategic thinking, process design, and data-driven
decision-making to solve real-world challenges and improve productivity in ethical and socially responsive ways.

III.	COURSE DESCRIPTION	:
This course provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the principles, strategies, and tools used in
managing operations within manufacturing and service organizations. It explores key topics such as operations strategy,
process design, capacity planning, supply chain management, inventory control, quality assurance, and project scheduling.
Emphasis is placed on applying quantitative and qualitative methods to solve real-world operational challenges, improve
productivity, and enhance organizational competitiveness. Through case studies, simulations, and team projects, students
will develop critical thinking and decision-making skills essential for effective operations leadership in dynamic business
environments.
Anchored in Marian and Augustinian values, this course introduces students to the principles and tools of managing
operations in manufacturing and service organizations. It emphasizes strategic thinking, process design, and data-driven
decision-making to solve real-world challenges and improve productivity in ethical and socially responsive ways.
